g.text: Two small Android apps that do one job each. Both
work offline, both ask for nothing but the files you hand
them, and both are signed with the same key so one
can hand you to the other.
One for glyphs, one for photos
Both free brands in your pocket: pick a glyph, set its weight, size and
background in a live preview, open the whole set in a scrolling sheet, copy
Pick photos, preview the result with a before/after slider, then compress.
Batch queue, resolution caps, metadata stripped, originals untouched.
The browser you can use here without installing is
page, its stylesheet, Poppins and both catalogs, wrapped in a WebView that
serves them from a private origin inside the app. Nothing is fetched, because
the app cannot fetch: there is no
A preview, three controls, one sheet
The chevron lists the brands — Lineicons and Coolicons — and each opens its own page with its own catalog.
The selected glyph sits in its own tab. Weight, size and surface repaint it as you press; the file itself never changes.
All 1,864 glyphs live behind one toggle and scroll inside their own sheet, so the page reads as a preview rather than a
Copy SVG hands over the exact file: 24×24 viewBox,
Both catalogs, the pages and the fonts travel inside the APK. One palette, Poppins, hairline rules — the same system as
publishes — bundled at build time by
Built for a Galaxy Z Flip 7 (Android 16). Signed, no third-party libraries, adaptive
launcher icon. The checksum is on the
Pick a level; the encoder retries lower until the file actually gets smaller.
Cap the longest edge at 1280, 1920, 2560, 3200 or 4096 px, or keep the original.
Up to 40 photos, per-file savings, then share them all in one go.
EXIF rotation is applied to the pixels, so portrait shots stay upright.
Location and device tags are dropped during re-encode.
Tapping a saved result reopens the slider so you can confirm the file matches the preview.

Android says the install is blocked: tap
. If Play Protect warns about an unknown developer, choose
Updating from an earlier build keeps your data — same signing key, higher version code.
These are self-signed builds, so Play Protect may call them unrecognised. That
is expected for apps installed outside the Play Store, not a sign of tampering.
No SDKs, no analytics, no network
Icons 2.3 · All brands in the app
The left pull-down opens with All, and the page behind it travels inside the APK: a tab per brand over a
sheet of twenty glyphs, one from each category, so the two sets can be read side by side with the radio
The zip estimate moved into the line under the Export button, where the running summary used to be, and
the collected glyphs now wrap into rows instead of running off the edge of the tab.
Double-tap a glyph in the sheet and it collects into a tab above it, with Remove selected and Remove all.
Add all takes the whole category, and a category change starts the selection clean. The line under the
preview estimates the zip before you press Export.
Format is a pull-down like the size: SVG, PNG, WEBP or JPG, one at a time, and the copy button renames itself to
match. The two lists never open together.
Your background choice now sticks per brand alongside the format and the size, so a white tile
survives a reload and the exports come back on white.
Icons 1.8 · One size, in a list
The export size is now a pull-down holding all six sizes from 32 to 1024px, instead of a row that had to squeeze.
What you pick still carries over to the zip.
Icons 1.7 · Sizes on two rows, and a pasteable PNG
The six export sizes now sit on two rows, so none of them is squeezed. The format and
size you pick are remembered per brand, and on the site copying a raster also puts a
PNG on the clipboard to paste straight into a design tool.
Icons 1.6 · Whole sets at any size
The export size now runs from 32 to 1024px, and one button packs every glyph the sheet shows into a
single zip, in the format you picked. Inside the app that zip lands in Downloads/Icons.
Copy hands over the SVG, or a 512px PNG, WEBP or JPG drawn on the black or white background. The app saves those to
The browser is inset below the status bar and a camera cutout, so the band is no longer clipped. A page the
app does not carry now offers the site address and an Open on the web button.
The preview tile is a black or white swatch now, labelled as such, instead of the palette’s field and band.
The category you picked last is restored the next time you open a brand, and All icons forgets it.
Both sets filter by their vendor's own categories — Coolicons' 30, Lineicons' 51 — beside the name filter. The weight
control now writes the chosen stroke onto every element, and fills the dots the stroke would otherwise turn inside out.
Both brands, 1,864 glyphs, bundled with the pages, the stylesheet and Poppins. WebView on a private origin so
and the clipboard behave exactly as they do on the site.
A preview tab with weight, size and background, and a copy button that hands over the untouched SVG.
All glyphs sit behind one toggle and scroll inside their own sheet instead of filling the page.
: the browser is inside the APK, so there is nothing to request.
Every heading, label and number is set in Poppins instead of the system font and its mono captions.
The app is indigo with band-grey actions and hairline rules where thick ink borders used to be.
The dark-mode toggle is gone because the design carries a single palette. Nothing else about compressing photos
